correctness.rationale: For every v>=0, k,p>0 and t>0 the two receiving-room Laplace resolvents are k^2/Dj(s), with D1-D2=pk(s+v). Both symmetric positive matrices have spectra strictly above v. The inverse product transform is a sixfold exponential convolution h>0, log-concave by the established Prékopa theorem, and analytically strictly log-concave because h~t^5/120 near zero. Its log derivative decreases from +infinity to -min lambda<-v, implying one and only one sign crossing. Direct integration proves strict positive cumulative difference and its v=0 boundary; exact reflection proves two-room identity. Reconstructed symbolic identities and independent matrix exponentials pass.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary full texts separately establish empirical purifier-placement effects and the multizone matrix framework but not the simultaneous unique crossover, all-horizon dose order, and sharp two-room obstruction. Classical log-concavity is acknowledged prior work. Accessible earlier claims and published research comparisons did not reveal direct implication. Historical priority is provisional.
residual_risks: General matrix semigroup/Markov-chain killing inequalities could have published specialized theorems implying the result even without indoor-air terminology; no exhaustive historical uniqueness claim.
Original Prékopa primary text was not inspected; the standard convolution-preservation theorem is used with attribution.
No attempt is made to extend strict comparisons to asymmetric flows, unequal volumes or filtration-induced airflow changes.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a physically motivated discrepancy among instantaneous downstream concentration, cumulative exposure, and step-source concentration, giving strict universal rank reversal for one metric yet uniform strict ranking for the others. The exactly minimal three-room setting and full v>=0 boundary are useful nontrivial benchmarks for validating multizone codes; the quantified result is not an empirical building recommendation.
